findings.reason: the fix is aimed at a mechanism the code does not run, so a node could land the enumeration and leave the 22% exactly where it is, which is the third consecutive time this plan's live check has not moved.
findings.text: §22 says the change token's `_misfiled_review_candidates` (22%) "enumerates the review store's index for each run", but `_misfiled_review_candidates` (`reckon/crew/recovery_memo.py:370–385`) only calls `review_module._store_index(directory)`, and `_store_index`/`_store_indexes` (`reckon/crew/review_records.py:1477–1509`, `:1572–1583`) hold a per-process cache keyed on the store directory's stat identity, re-listing only when that identity moves; per run it is one `stat` and a dict lookup, so the per-run enumeration the section blames does not exist

findings.reason: the section must either state that the annotation inputs join the cache key or scope the cache to the parse and keep annotation per tick; without that, a node can satisfy the done-when and still either not move the measure or make promotion read a stale added-failure count.
findings.text: the deliverable keeps "each record's per-file identity" and answers `_stored_review`/`select_review_for_head` from the tick's enumeration, but the value `read_review` returns is not a function of the review-store file alone: `read_review` (`reckon/crew/review.py:3759`) ends in `annotate_review_of_run`, which reads the reviewed run's `manifest.md` and the two gate logs it names on every call and stamps `added_failure_count`; a cache keyed only on review-store identities therefore either still pays those two or three per-run reads every tick (no busy-share improvement) or serves a stale `added_failure_count` when a gate log gains a failure

findings.reason: as written the test's enumeration assertion passes on the unfixed code, so the only falsifiable half is the `read_review` count and the section's stated mechanism goes unmeasured.
findings.text: the head assertion's first clause requires that a tick "enumerates the store directory once", which is already true at base for the only path the section names, since `_store_indexes` lists a store directory once per stat-identity change and not per run; the clause therefore cannot distinguish head from base and measures none of the deliverable's first half

findings.reason: a later reader, or the node that has to decide whether the landed change moved the cost, cannot open or re-derive the profile, so the section's evidence is a number with no artifact behind it.
findings.text: every percentage §22's argument rests on (51% in the publish, 82% within it, 36% in the change token, 22% `_misfiled_review_candidates`, 51% `stat`, 13% `scandir`) comes from a "75 s py-spy profile" that names no path, while the busy-share log beside it is named in full
